title: MacWhisper vs Typeless on Mac in 2026: which one fits your dictation and transcripts
metaTitle: MacWhisper vs Typeless on Mac in 2026: Price, Privacy, Features
description: MacWhisper vs Typeless compared on price, privacy, platforms and dictation. Find out which Mac app fits your files, meetings and daily typing.
intro: MacWhisper and Typeless both turn speech into text on a Mac, but they are built for different work. MacWhisper suits you if you transcribe files and record meetings, and its Pro license is a one-time €64. Typeless suits you if you dictate across many apps and devices, and its Pro plan costs $12 per member per month when billed yearly.
tldr: MacWhisper: a one-time €64 Pro license, with file transcription and meeting recording on your Mac.
Typeless: a free plan with limited words, and Pro at $12 per member per month billed yearly.
Privacy: MacWhisper says sensitive content can stay on your Mac. Typeless says it discards audio after processing.
Lazur is a third option: a voice assistant with dictation included, not a file transcriber.

blocks.text: Who each app is built for

MacWhisper is built around files and recordings. Its site leads with transcribing mp3, wav, m4a, mov and mp4 files on your Mac. It also records from the microphone, handles batches and pulls audio from YouTube and other media links. System-wide dictation is in there too, but it is not the headline.

Typeless is built around dictation. Its homepage talks about a voice keyboard that cleans up speech in any app. It lists filler-word removal, auto-formatting, a personal dictionary and per-app tone. It also runs on Windows, Linux, iOS and Android. The official MacWhisper site does not list other platforms.

Here is the short version. If your week includes audio files, start with MacWhisper. If your week includes a lot of typing, start with Typeless. If you mostly want help working inside your Mac apps, Lazur is the third option, and it is covered further down.
MacWhisper pricing and Typeless pricing compared

MacWhisper has a free tier that its site describes as free forever, at €0. Pro is a one-time €64 license with lifetime updates. You can buy it through the Gumroad page or the App Store. The site warns about scam sites that copy the official site, so check the address before you enter a card.

items: MacWhisper Pro, pay once, €64 per license, with lifetime updates
Typeless Free, $0 per member per month, with limited words
Typeless Pro, $12 per member per month billed yearly, or $30 billed monthly
Typeless Enterprise, custom pricing, with SSO, SCIM and audit logs

blocks.text: Typeless charges by the month or the year, and the difference matters. At $12 a month billed yearly, Pro comes to $144 for a year. Billed monthly at $30, the same plan comes to $360 for a year. MacWhisper Pro is €64 once. The two bills use different currencies, so do not add them as if they were equal. This page does not convert euros to dollars.

Two pricing mistakes come up often. The first is comparing a one-time license to a subscription after only one month. The second is assuming the Typeless free plan covers a full workday. Its page says Limited words and gives no number. Third-party sites quote figures that do not agree, so check the limit in your own account first.
Transcribing files and recordings

MacWhisper accepts mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, opus, mov and mp4 files. You add a file and get a transcript. Speaker recognition labels who is talking. The site says it covers about 100 languages. For a long interview, speaker labels are the feature you will notice first.

Exports cover SRT, VTT, TXT, MD, PDF, HTML, DOTE and DOCX. Subtitle files and Word documents are both covered. Power users get watched folders, a command line tool, and links to Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, n8n, Make.com and webhooks. You can also point MacWhisper at your own API key or at a local model through Ollama or LM Studio.

Typeless does not show file transcription on its homepage or pricing page. Its feature list focuses on live dictation. If you need to turn a folder of interviews into text, check its feature list before you assume it can do that job.

Here is a common case. You have a recorded interview, and you need a transcript with speaker labels. MacWhisper covers that workflow directly. Typeless is a weak fit for that step. Lazur is not a file transcriber either, because its listed features do not include file transcription.
Mac dictation: typing with your voice

Both apps type into any app with a cursor. MacWhisper adds automatic grammar improvement and app-specific AI prompts. Typeless adds filler-word removal, auto-formatting, a personal dictionary and per-app tone. A competing app review calls Typeless filler-word and self-correction handling genuinely good. That is an opinion from a rival, so test it on your own speech.

Accuracy depends on the room. The same competing review says Typeless accuracy drops in noisy environments, and it says Typeless has no offline mode. Those are opinions too, but they are easy to test. Dictate in the room where you actually work, with the fan and the street noise you really have.

Speed claims need a careful read. Typeless's homepage says dictation is 4x faster than typing, with 220 words per minute for its voice keyboard against 45 for QWERTY. That is the company's own figure. An independent lab study on arXiv, 1608.07323, found English speech entry at 153 words per minute against 52 by keyboard. That study tested phones in a lab, not these two apps.

Typing research adds some context. A CHI 2018 paper, Observations on Typing from 136 Million Keystrokes, drew on 168,000 volunteers. It measured typing, not dictation, so use it as background only. Your own speed on your own text is the number that matters for your decision.
Meetings, calls and recordings

MacWhisper records meetings in Zoom, Teams, Webex, Skype, Chime and Discord. It can start and stop recording on its own when it detects a call. A competing app review lists meeting recording and speaker separation as beta features, so test them before an important client call.
Typeless does not list meeting recording on its homepage or pricing page. If you need a written record of calls, MacWhisper is the app to test first. Keep Typeless for what you say at your keyboard.
Privacy and where your audio goes

MacWhisper's site says it processes sensitive content locally, and that data never leaves your Mac. It also says it uses local models to transcribe your files. Those are the site's words. Treat them as a claim to test, and check which engine you picked in settings.

Here is the catch. MacWhisper also supports your own API key and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. If you connect a cloud API, your audio goes to that provider. A local model through Ollama or LM Studio keeps the audio on your Mac. Choose the engine on purpose before you transcribe client files.

Typeless's privacy policy says it operates under a zero data retention policy. Audio and context are processed in real time and discarded after the results return. History cloud sync can keep your history text until you delete it. Feedback corrections are used for training only with explicit opt-in consent.

The homepage goes further. It says dictation data is never used for model training, by the company or by third parties. It also claims ISO 27001, GDPR and HIPAA compliance. The privacy policy confirms GDPR scope but does not mention ISO 27001 or HIPAA. Treat the certification claims as unverified until you see them in writing.

The same competing review describes an unverified reverse-engineering analysis of Typeless. That analysis reports window-title collection and clipboard access. The review says no public rebuttal exists. Read it as one side of a dispute, and ask Typeless directly for its data flows.

If you handle health, legal or client material, ask both vendors for their data processing terms in writing. Do not rely on a badge on a homepage. Read the policy, check the storage settings, and confirm where the audio is processed.
Platforms and where each app runs

MacWhisper is a Mac app. Its site does not show a minimum macOS version, so check the System Requirements FAQ on macwhisper.com before you buy. The site also does not confirm Intel support. Check both on the official site before you pay.

Typeless lists macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android. If your work moves between a Mac, a Windows PC and a phone, Typeless covers more ground. Cloud sync across devices is part of the Pro plan, according to its pricing page.
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned but not available. If you need one assistant on your Windows laptop, Lazur is not an option yet.
A common mistake is buying for the Mac on your desk and forgetting the Windows laptop you use on the train. List every device you will dictate on, then check each app against that list.
Where Lazur fits in this comparison

Lazur is a third option. It is not a file transcriber. It is a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. It answers out loud and draws a circle and a label around the thing you ask about.

Lazur also dictates. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots come with it. Dictation is unlimited on both Lazur plans. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you.

Pricing for Lazur is Pro at $18 per month, or $15 per month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Power is $120 per month, or $96 per month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. The 3-day Pro trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card.

If you keep asking how to do things in apps you rarely use, Lazur fits better than either dictation app. Ask Lazur to walk you through it. It guides you one click at a time and waits for each click before it moves on. Lazur circles the button, but you do the clicking.
Which one should you pick

items: Pick MacWhisper if you transcribe audio or video files, record meetings and want to pay once.
Pick Typeless if you dictate into many apps, work across Mac, Windows or a phone, and accept a subscription.
Pick Lazur if you want voice help inside your Mac apps, with dictation included and no file work.
Start with the free plans if you are unsure. Test with your own audio and your own sentences.

blocks.text: Before you pay, run a short test on your real work. Give yourself a few days. Use the same audio or sentences in each app, and keep notes on the errors.

items: Install MacWhisper Free from macwhisper.com and transcribe one recording you already have.
Open the Typeless free plan and dictate the same short email you would send at work.
Turn on microphone access under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone for each app.
Count the words you had to fix in each transcript and each draft email.
If you want voice help too, start the 3-day Lazur trial and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask a question about your screen.

blocks.text: For a wider look at other options, read [Typeless alternatives for Mac](/alternatives/typeless). To measure how fast you speak and type, try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).
Common mistakes when comparing these apps

items: Trusting vendor speed claims. The 220 words per minute figure is Typeless's own marketing.
Mixing currencies. €64 and $12 are not the same unit, and this page does not convert them.
Mixing product listings. An App Store app called Whisper Transcription is a separate product with different pricing.
Reading only the homepage. Check the privacy policy, the storage settings and the engine you use.
Missing permissions. macOS needs microphone access, and often Accessibility access, before dictation works. Find Accessibility under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility.

blocks.text: Grant the permissions once, then run your test. Many first-day problems come from a missing permission rather than the app itself. Fix that first, then judge the transcript quality.

faq.question: Is MacWhisper free?
faq.answer: MacWhisper has a free plan, and its official site lists it at €0 and free forever. MacWhisper Pro is a one-time €64 license with lifetime updates. Check macwhisper.com for what the free plan includes before you rely on it for long files.

faq.question: How much does Typeless cost?
faq.answer: Typeless has a Free plan at $0 per member per month with limited words. Pro costs $12 per member per month billed yearly, or $30 billed monthly, with unlimited words. Enterprise is custom pricing. These figures come from its pricing page, checked 2026-11-09.

faq.question: Does MacWhisper work without internet?
faq.answer: The official site says it uses local models and that sensitive content never leaves your Mac. It does not state plainly that every setup works offline. If you need offline use, turn off Wi-Fi and test one file before a trip.

faq.question: Which is more private, MacWhisper or Typeless?
faq.answer: Neither is automatically safer. MacWhisper keeps local model work on your Mac, but it sends audio to any cloud API you connect. Typeless says audio is discarded after processing, and its history sync can keep text until you delete it. Compare both policies against your own rules.

faq.question: Can Typeless transcribe audio files?
faq.answer: Its homepage and pricing page list live dictation features, not file imports. Check its feature list before you buy it for transcripts. If you need file transcription, MacWhisper is the app built for that job.

faq.question: Does Lazur transcribe files or record meetings?
faq.answer: No. Lazur's listed features cover dictation, voice help, everyday actions and research in Chrome. It does not list file transcription or meeting recording. For those jobs, test MacWhisper first.

faq.question: Which of these apps works on Windows?
faq.answer: Typeless lists Windows, Linux, iOS and Android. MacWhisper's official site lists a Mac app only. Lazur runs on macOS, with Windows planned but not available.

verdict: Pick MacWhisper if you need file transcription and meeting recording on your Mac, and you want to pay once. Pick Typeless if you dictate all day into many apps, or you work across Mac, Windows and phones, and you accept a subscription. Lazur is the third option for voice help inside your apps. It is not the tool for transcripts.
